subject: SDK compatibility checklist + prefetch/backpressure mitigation for BrightLane POC
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Amy Chen <amy.chen@brightlane.com>
Date: 2026-04-12T09:12:00Z
Subject: SDK compatibility checklist + prefetch/backpressure mitigation for BrightLane POC

Hi team —

Quick summary: BrightLane hit intermittent 500s during our last POC run when they exercised high-concurrency streaming with a long prefix. They called out two actionable asks from their side: (1) an SDK-level guardrail we can ship quickly to avoid client-side replay + duplicate side-effects, and (2) a short-term runtime mitigation for observed prefetch/backpressure stalls.

Marissa — can you confirm the customer timeline? They want the fix or a stable workaround before next Tue's exec demo.

Dev / Karthik — from logs they shared (attached runtime-dump-20260411.txt) we see a burst of prefetched KV entries followed by a backlog spike and several 502/500s reported by their client. We need:
- A minimal SDK change (opt-in) to enforce an idempotency token per request + client reconnect backoff jitter; this should be small and patchable.
- A runtime config we can flip per-customer to reduce speculative prefetch aggressiveness (or throttle prefetch per-connection) so that BrightLane's concurrency profile doesn't saturate the kernel.

Amy — appreciate the logs. If you can also confirm which model variant you pinned (and your max concurrent streams per host) that helps.

Goal for this thread: produce a short mutual action plan (MAP) with owners and a timeline. If we can scope a quick SDK patch and a runtime toggle by EOD Monday, we can get BrightLane to green for the demo.

Thanks,
Tessa

--
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Amy Chen <amy.chen@brightlane.com>
Date: 2026-04-12T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: SDK compatibility checklist + prefetch/backpressure mitigation for BrightLane POC

Thanks Tessa — looping in a few runtime details.

Quick take after an initial pass on runtime-dump-20260411.txt:
- Prefetch explosion looks correlated with long prefix reuse across concurrent streams; KV cache pressure goes up and kernel queues backlogged requests.
- We saw a handful of "prefetch task" worker crashes logged as soft OOMs; these will surface as internal 5xx to the client.

Short-term runtime mitigations (can be toggled per-customer):
1) prefetch_window_limit: cap speculative prefetch to N tokens per-connection (we can set to 64 instead of 1024)
2) prefetch_rate_limit: limit spawn rate of prefetch workers under high concurrency
3) aggressive_kv_eviction: apply earlier eviction during spike (may slightly increase cold-token latency)

These are config flags; I can stage a toggle for BrightLane in staging and coordinate a quick rollout to prod if we get sign-off. However we should also fix the SDK to reduce client retries that amplify the load.

SDK ask (minimal patch):
- Add optional parameter `idempotency_key` that, when present, deduplicates server-side operations for the lifetime of a request-id window. This is small and avoids application-level duplicates when reconnects occur.
- Add default reconnect strategy with exponential backoff + jitter in the JS/py SDKs (opt-in for now).

Estimated effort: prefetch toggles = config + small release (~2 engineer-days to test + 1 for rollout coordination). SDK patch = ~2 engineer-days across SDKs for a conservative rollout.

Action items:
- Dev: prototype staging toggle for prefetch_window_limit and run BrightLane load profile (target: EOD Monday to have a staging verification).
- Karthik: help validate kernel/driver-level logs (I suspect quantization-specific kernel path might make memory usage noisier for their model variant).
- Marissa/Tessa: confirm BrightLane can accept a short freeze on prefetch (we may trade off cold latency).

I'll attach the runtime dump we analyzed (runtime-dump-20260411.txt).

--
Dev
Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Amy Chen <amy.chen@brightlane.com>

Date: 2026-04-13T08:34:00Z
Subject: Re: SDK compatibility checklist + prefetch/backpressure mitigation for BrightLane POC

Thanks — appreciate the quick analysis. A couple clarifications from our side:
- We pinned `redwood/opt-13b:v2` for latency reasons. Concurrency: our baseline test uses 40 concurrent streaming clients per host, but the exec demo will push ~80 for 90s.
- We do use aggressive client reconnects on our current SDK that may replay chunks when a stream fails.

We can accept a short freeze on speculative prefetch for the demo if it prevents the 5xx behavior. Timeline: the exec demo is on Tue 2026-04-14 at 16:00 PT — ideally we have a prod toggle ready to flip at least 2 hours prior.

I'll run another capture for a model-level trace and share if helpful.

Amy
Director, Engineering — BrightLane
